Von: National Centre for Statistical Ecology Members Mailing List <NC...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK> im Auftrag von Eleni Matechou <00014031ee1a45e...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK>
Gesendet: Dienstag, 3. November 2026 15:05
An: NC...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK <NC...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK>
Betreff: Leverhulme PhD project to forward to contacts

Dear all

Would it be possible to forward this information to potential PhD students or to keep in mind when advising students looking for PhD projects?

Cheers!
Eleni

Living with gulls: modelling how our waste shapes the lives of gulls and people
This is a four-year, fully funded Leverhulme Living with Waste scholarship, with a substantial conference and travel budget. The student will join a cohort of doctoral researchers and receive broad interdisciplinary training.
The project will develop spatio-temporal statistical models for multi-source data to understand how waste shapes where gulls live and which communities live with them. The models will be used to quantify how landfill operations and urban food waste have shifted gulls between coast, landfill and town; identify which communities live with gulls, and how this relates to deprivation, housing and waste services; and assess whether changes to waste management could reduce human-gull conflict without displacing it or harming gull populations. Gulls cost councils substantial sums, are in decline, and the impacts of their urban presence fall unevenly. How waste drives these three dynamics is poorly understood.
The student will gain skills in statistical modelling, data integration and machine learning, valued in academia, government and industry, and apply them to a growing question: how decisions about waste change the way people and wildlife share space. The interdisciplinary training offered through the Living with Waste school, and co-supervision by human and cultural geographers, will equip the student with qualitative skills and the ability to situate the research within social scientific, political and humanist debates on human-nonhuman relations in urban contexts.
Information about the project  https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/hss/research/postgraduate-research-student-funding-opportunities/leverhulme-living-with-waste-doctoral-programme/projects-and-supervisors/2026-4-year-call/living-with-gulls/
Information about the Living with Waste Leverhulme Doctoral Programme
https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/hss/research/postgraduate-research-student-funding-opportunities/leverhulme-living-with-waste-doctoral-programme/

Information about how to apply  https://www.qmul.ac.uk/about/hss/research/postgraduate-research-student-funding-opportunities/leverhulme-living-with-waste-doctoral-programme/how-to-apply/

Please forward this information to potential applicants and ask them to contact me (Dr Eleni Matechou e.mat...@qmul.ac.uk) if they would like to find out more about the project or the doctoral programme.
Eleni Matechou (she/her)

Reader in Statistics

School of Mathematical Sciences

Queen Mary University of London

Email: e.mat...@qmul.ac.uk

Betreff: Fellowship in New World Screwworm Modeling and Surveillance (Closes End Nov 2026)

Colleagues,

We are seeking three quantitative ecologists with modeling experience (mathematical/Bayesian) and interest in applying models to provide practical guidance for New World Screwworm surveillance, especially in wildlife.

We are reviewing candidates as they apply and hope to have people on board this before the end of the year.

Please distribute.

Apply here -> https://www.zintellect.com/Opportunity/Details/USDA-APHIS-2026-0421
